title: Build source-pinned Solid 2 RC13 foundations with parallel, exclusive ownership
description: WHY: Establish the architecture for a fresh React Base UI port directly to Solid 2.0.0-rc.13, not an upgrade of any old Solid port. The sole behavioral upstream is /Users/avi/avir-oss/ref/base-ui at 19511bb171f3b360b006c94cf6d07e53cb446505, verified before planning. READ FIRST: packages/react/package.json, packages/react/src/index.ts, packages/react/src/floating-ui-react/index.ts and the sourcePaths of each child. IMPLEMENT: Deliver the sixteen requested foundation domains plus floating-core, temporal and media-query as independently schedulable tasks. External bsolid-bootstrap owns package scaffolding, coordinated RC13 pins, root types, shared structural contracts, package exports and integration barrels; bsolid-harness owns runner infrastructure and publishes exact typecheck, unit, SSR/hydration and browser commands. Children depend on concrete prerequisites, never this epic. Initial independent lanes are dom, lifecycle, filter and temporal; events then state/render/providers unlock later work. Use one packages/solid package, with framework-independent helpers in src/utils and no React utils runtime dependency. All hooks become internal createX primitives; exported legacy hook-shaped subpaths receive explicit bootstrap-approved mappings, not forgotten exports. Controlled state derives from live accessors plus a local uncontrolled initial snapshot; cancellation precedes commit. Effects use createEffect(compute,effect), return cleanup and extract reactive inputs in compute. Refs execute ownerless: create their resources and teardown in setup. Treat ordinary writes as staged; pass next values to imperative work explicitly. Context itself is the provider; required contexts are defaultless, optional ones explicitly null. No blanket ownedWrite, diagnostic suppression, deep-proxied DOM nodes or routine flush. WRITE BOUNDARY: owns patterns are exclusive allowlists; a file-stem glob includes its colocated tests/specs, and directory globs include only that subtree. Each child owns its named tracking JSON. Shared manifests, lockfiles, internals/types.ts, types/**, floating-ui-react/types.ts, floating-ui-react/index.ts and floating-ui-react/utils.ts remain main-owned. NON-GOALS: public component families, final browser suite execution, old-port compatibility and upstream modifications. VALIDATE: require each child to map source test titles to translated cases and actual harness commands; retain browser-only cases with deferred status and replay instructions. Audit runtime imports as a DAG using leaf imports, export-seam handoffs and pairwise write ownership before integration. Document any impossible parity seam rather than inventing a substitute.
acceptance: All nineteen child tasks have unique write allowlists, existing upstream sourcePaths and an acyclic prerequisite graph containing only task IDs and the two external prerequisites.
Bootstrap receives a mapping for every foundation-related package export, including temporal adapters, unstable media query and hook-shaped internals; root export wiring stays main-owned.
No foundation runtime imports a public component family, React, react-dom, use-sync-external-store or @base-ui/utils.
Each child records source-translated cases, exact executed commands, framework adaptations and retained deferred browser cases in its owned tracking JSON.
State, effects, refs, rendering, contexts, geometry and hydration gates use verified RC13 public APIs without blanket diagnostic suppression.

title: Port realm-safe DOM, platform and pure utility leaves
description: WHY: DOM traversal, realm checks and resource cleanup are shared by controls, floating interactions and portals. A single framework-independent leaf layer prevents subtly different Shadow DOM and iframe behavior from being copied into each family. Canonical source is /Users/avi/avir-oss/ref/base-ui at 19511bb171f3b360b006c94cf6d07e53cb446505; this is a fresh Solid 2 RC13 port. READ FIRST: packages/utils/src/shadowDom.ts, owner.ts, addEventListener.ts, mergeCleanups.ts and platform/index.ts; then packages/react/src/floating-ui-react/utils/element.ts, tabbable.ts, markOthers.ts and their existing tests. IMPLEMENT: Copy pure algorithms with import adaptation into the single target package. Preserve closest traversal through assigned slots and shadow hosts, nested activeElement resolution, composedPath targeting with post-dispatch fallback, owner-document/window lookup and realm-safe element checks. Carry over listener options and exact removal symmetry, cleanup composition, disabled element detection, form submitter selection, arithmetic/equality helpers, immutable empty constants and error/warn formatting. DOM utility imports must remain safe during SSR; do not eagerly resolve document, navigator or window at module scope. Also own the low-level tabbable, focus queue, markOthers, floating element/attribute/constants helpers, measurement and scroll geometry leaves so portal and focus workers can consume them without importing one another. Extract isElementVisible from upstream floating utils/composite.ts into owned utils/visibility.ts; tabbable imports that leaf, never composite's higher-level navigation module. Replace element.ts's PopupTriggerMap type import with bootstrap's structural trigger-lookup contract and its TooltipTriggerDataAttributes runtime import with an exact shared constant, preserving the source attribute string. Preserve original attributes and reference-counted restoration where several layers share an element. Keep raw DOM nodes and observer objects outside deep stores. WRITE BOUNDARY: only the listed utils/platform subtree, individual utility stems, floating low-level utility stems, internals/constants.ts and internals/noop.ts, plus dom coverage JSON. No floating interaction hooks, scroll-lock lifecycle, event preventability, IDs or context implementations belong here. NON-GOALS: generic DOM framework, browser polyfill package, public components, geometry middleware, React version/safeReact shims, or porting testUtils runtime. VALIDATE: translate the upstream helper tests and add cross-realm/ShadowRoot fixtures where the source behavior requires them. Run the commands published by bsolid-harness for these files and server import safety. Retain browser-dependent tabbability/layout cases as translated deferred tests rather than deleting or pretending jsdom proves them. Record every unported React-only helper and its replacement owner in the coverage handoff.
acceptance: Composed-tree closest/contains/activeElement/getTarget cases include slots, nested shadow roots and post-dispatch targets.
Iframe-owned nodes use their own document/window constructors; server import never touches unavailable browser globals.
Listener and markOthers cleanup restores preexisting attributes exactly and is safe under overlapping consumers.
Tabbable and measurement source cases are translated; layout-only cases remain explicitly deferred for final browser replay.
No React dependency, deep DOM proxy or import from a higher-level foundation is introduced.

title: Define controlled accessors and staged local state without React stores
description: WHY: ReactStore's prop synchronization, subscription snapshots and render scheduling are not Solid architecture. This task supplies the small state primitives that let independently ported controls preserve behavior without installing a React compatibility runtime. Source of truth is /Users/avi/avir-oss/ref/base-ui at 19511bb171f3b360b006c94cf6d07e53cb446505; target is Solid 2 RC13. READ FIRST: packages/utils/src/useControlled.ts and its test/spec files, store/Store.ts, store/ReactStore.ts, store/useStore.ts, createSelector.ts and createSelectorMemoized.ts; also internals/useValueChanged.ts and utils/NullStore.ts. IMPLEMENT: Expose createControlled with an accessor for the external value, a one-time untracked default snapshot and a local signal for uncontrolled state. Preserve initial controlled-mode selection, defined-default overloads, undefined fallback and development mode-switch/default-change warnings. The effective value is a memo/accessor, never a prop copied into state by an effect. Separate request/change from commit: resolve the proposed value explicitly, call the current consumer callback with event details, inspect isCanceled, then stage local writes only when the selected mode permits them. Controlled requests do not fabricate acknowledgement. Document successive same-turn updater semantics and pass explicit transaction values into imperative consumers instead of rereading stale accessors. Provide narrowly scoped signal-backed model/select helpers only where consumers actually need them; migrate immutable selector semantics without recreating ReactStore, useSyncExternalStore, force-render counters or a generic subscription framework. Stable callback wrappers read current callbacks at invocation. createValueChanged tracks the upstream observation boundary with split effects, and NullStore becomes an inert structural implementation of bootstrap's contract. Publish examples showing request-time values versus committed reactive values for both signal and draft-store consumers. WRITE BOUNDARY: utils/state/**, createControlled.*, createPreviousValue.*, internals/createValueChanged.* and utils/NullStore.*, with state coverage JSON. Bootstrap owns shared type contracts; popup and floating models remain in their own tasks. NON-GOALS: application stores, effect-synced props, optimistic controlled updates, global flushing, deep proxying elements, or blanket ownedWrite. VALIDATE: translate source state/type cases and add cancellation-before-commit, parent rejection, prop replacement and batched request cases using the harness's actual scheduler. Keep framework-specific adaptations explained alongside source test titles; do not assert React render counts as Solid behavior.
acceptance: Controlled reads follow live props directly; uncontrolled defaults are captured once and never effect-synchronized.
Canceled changes cause neither local commit nor downstream transaction side effects; controlled callbacks can decline updates.
Initial-mode warnings and defined/undefined overloads match the source contract, including disappearing controlled values.
Same-turn requests use documented explicit next-value semantics without ordinary production flush calls.
No ReactStore/useSyncExternalStore imitation, reactive DOM proxy or diagnostic blanket is present.
Translated state suites and type fixtures pass with source case mappings and actual harness commands recorded.

title: Build live render callbacks, state attributes and identity-preserving host rendering
description: WHY: Every part needs one Solid-native rendering contract. Mechanically cloning JSX or recomputing a subtree whenever state changes would lose focus, selection, uncontrolled input contents and registrations. The sole behavioral source is /Users/avi/avir-oss/ref/base-ui at 19511bb171f3b360b006c94cf6d07e53cb446505, ported fresh to Solid 2 RC13. READ FIRST: internals/useRenderElement.tsx, its test/spec files, use-render/useRender.ts, internals/getStateAttributesProps.ts, stateAttributesMapping.ts, resolveRenderedId.ts and utils/resolveClassName.ts/resolveStyle.ts. IMPLEMENT: Build createRenderElement and the public createRender facade against bootstrap's Solid JSX types. A render callback receives stable live props and getter-backed state, and returns Solid JSX; an already-created JSX value is not a cloneable React element. Use RC13's supported dynamic host API for changing tags, keeping host/component identity stable when only ordinary state, classes, handlers or attributes change. Preserve default button type, image alt, enabled=false behavior, state-to-data attributes, custom mapping overrides and render callback precedence. Use native class, including RC13 class representations supported by bootstrap, rather than className/classList; retain Base UI's right-to-left external class precedence through the events-owned merge implementation. Native attributes use RC13 spelling. Forward children lazily and merge callback refs through lifecycle's setup-owned utility, avoiding element recreation or reactive primitive creation inside ref application. resolveRenderedId must inspect the final live ID contract rather than React element internals, including an explicit undefined override that removes a generated ID. WRITE BOUNDARY: render-element and state-attribute stems, render resolution utilities, use-render/** and render coverage JSON only. Events owns merge-props/**; lifecycle owns merged refs and IDs; bootstrap owns internals/types.ts, types/** and package export wiring. NON-GOALS: React element/lazy-wrapper compatibility, component implementations, custom JSX runtime, portals or global registration. VALIDATE: translate conformance, render and type cases to the harness. Prove callback state/props update while the same input node retains value, selection and focus, and that changing the actual render target disposes precisely once. Run available unit/type/SSR checks, retain hydration/browser identity cases for final replay, and document the deliberate callback-only adaptation for upstream element-valued render tests.
acceptance: State, class, style, ARIA and handlers remain live without re-running component setup or replacing the same host node.
Render callbacks receive typed live props/state; pre-created JSX cloning and React lazy introspection are absent.

Default button/img props, custom data mappings and enabled=false behavior have translated regression coverage; transition mappings import the bootstrap type-only union and render-owned TransitionStatusDataAttributes, never presence implementation.
Explicit undefined ID overrides mask generated defaults; render ID consumers see the final resolved value.
Ref replacement/disposal is exactly once and creates no effects or cleanup scopes in the callback.
Public facade and internals export mappings are handed to main; source type/conformance cases and deferred browser identity cases are inventoried.

title: Port native cancellation, reason details and Base UI prop merging
description: WHY: Base UI exposes two independent cancellation systems and special prop merging. Replacing either with Solid merge or defaultPrevented changes component composition and controlled behavior. Canonical upstream is /Users/avi/avir-oss/ref/base-ui at 19511bb171f3b360b006c94cf6d07e53cb446505; target this fresh port at Solid 2 RC13. READ FIRST: merge-props/mergeProps.ts and mergeProps.test.ts, internals/createBaseUIEventDetails.ts and its spec, reasons.ts/reason-parts.ts, packages/utils/src/useEnhancedClickHandler.ts and floating-ui-react/utils/event.ts. IMPLEMENT: Port reason-to-native-event discriminated types and createChangeEventDetails/createGenericEventDetails. details.cancel/isCanceled and allowPropagation/isPropagationAllowed retain their own mutable transaction flags. Separately make native DOM events preventable with preventBaseUIHandler/baseUIHandlerPrevented, including a single handler and first-position handler. Do not require React's nativeEvent marker; use realm-safe event recognition without wrapping away currentTarget or composedPath. defaultPrevented alone does not cancel every Base UI handler, although specific source algorithms may still inspect it. Port mergeProps/mergePropsN with rightmost ordinary prop precedence, right-to-left event execution and class ordering, rightmost style-key precedence and no implicit ref merging. Explicit undefined masks ordinary defaults; preserve upstream special handling of undefined event handlers and class/style merges rather than conflating all keys. Function prop getters receive the accumulated left-to-right props and remain responsible for their own chaining/cancellation checks. Use getter-backed reads and stable event dispatch wrappers so changing a consumer callback is observed despite RC13's bind-once direct event expressions. Port enhanced click interaction detection, modifier-preserving dispatch and mixed-toggle native behavior here. Arbitrary value callbacks must still run both handlers and must not acquire DOM-event prevention fields accidentally. WRITE BOUNDARY: merge-props/**, listed event-detail/reason/event utility stems and events coverage JSON. Bootstrap owns shared JSX/event type facades; composite owns createButton, and no events module imports composite, state or popup. NON-GOALS: synthetic event shim, React event pooling, built-in Solid merge equivalence, automatic ref merging or public button implementation. VALIDATE: translate merge and event specs, including undefined, function getter and primitive callback cases, then exercise native keyboard/pointer events, iframe events and changed handler props. Record exact harness commands and keep platform-only interaction cases as explicit deferred browser tests.
acceptance: Native events expose Base UI handler prevention independently of defaultPrevented and change-details cancellation.
Handler order, return value, class precedence, style overwrite and ordinary explicit undefined behavior match source tests.
Undefined handler exceptions and function-getter manual chaining are tested separately from ordinary prop masking.
A changed callback is invoked on the existing element without rebinding or stale setup snapshots.
Reason/detail type fixtures preserve event narrowing and custom properties without React event types.
No events-to-state/composite/popup import cycle or Solid merge substitution exists.

title: Implement owned resources, refs, hydration state and verified stable IDs
description: WHY: Timers, callback refs and IDs must follow Solid ownership instead of React render/effect lifetimes. This independent lane provides the verified primitives that unlock rendering, labels and portals. Canonical behavior comes from /Users/avi/avir-oss/ref/base-ui at 19511bb171f3b360b006c94cf6d07e53cb446505; use Solid 2 RC13 only. READ FIRST: packages/utils/src/useTimeout.ts, useAnimationFrame.ts, useIdleCallback.ts, useInterval.ts, useMergedRefs.ts, useStableCallback.ts, hydration.ts and useId.ts; internals/useBaseUiId.ts, RequestQueue.ts and TimeoutManager.ts. IMPLEMENT: Create setup-owned timeout/frame/idle/interval primitives and current-callback closures, preserving restart, clear, disposal and fallback semantics. Retain pure RequestQueue explicit settlement, concurrency and duplicate-key behavior, and keyed TimeoutManager semantics. Ref application is ownerless: it may assign the current raw element and apply imperative work, but must not create an effect or register onCleanup/onSettled there. Compose refs using resources created in setup; detach replaced elements and dispose once even when the renderer does not send a React-style null callback. Use split createEffect(compute,effect) with returned cleanup and supported onSettled lifecycle boundaries. Determine hydration state using public RC13 exports, not React external-store shims. STABLE-ID PROOF GATE: do not assume createUniqueId was removed. Inspection found https://unpkg.com/solid-js@2.0.0-rc.13/types/index.d.ts re-exports ./client/component.js, whose declaration explicitly exports createUniqueId(): string; https://v2.solidjs.com/reference/solid-js/components-context/create-unique-id documents hydration stability. Verify the pinned local package's browser/server runtime exports as well as declarations before selecting this public mechanism. Prove matching IDs across SSR/hydration, async ownership, multiple roots and concurrent requests; stop and document a blocker if the actual pinned build disagrees. Never substitute global counters, random UUIDs, private owner IDs or React17's fallback. Preserve explicit override and base-ui prefix semantics. Test empty-string overrides independently from omitted values so an intentional rendered ID override is not replaced by fallback truthiness. WRITE BOUNDARY: only listed lifecycle/ID/ref utility stems, queue/timeout internals and lifecycle coverage JSON. NON-GOALS: presence state machines, providers, prehydration script rendering, React hook emulation or automatic flushing. VALIDATE: translate timer/ref/ID tests, execute unit/type and minimal hydration proof through harness, retain broader browser cases for final replay and record API evidence URLs with the installed package version.
acceptance: The ID implementation has recorded RC13 public declaration/runtime evidence and a passing SSR/hydration proof, or is explicitly blocked without a fallback counter.
ID overrides, generated prefixes, concurrent requests and multiple roots have collision/mismatch checks.
Ownerless ref callbacks create no effects or cleanup registrations; replacement and disposal release each attachment exactly once.
Timers, animation frames, idle fallback, intervals and keyed managers leave no work after disposal.
RequestQueue tests preserve explicit settlement and concurrency behavior rather than auto-settling successful requests.
Effects are split with returned cleanup; no removed lifecycle API, React shim or blanket diagnostic suppression is used.

title: Port transition status, animation completion and retained mounting
description: WHY: Presence is distinct from requested open state; removing a closing node too early breaks exit animation, focus return and completion callbacks. The fresh Solid 2 RC13 implementation must preserve source lifecycle outcomes without copying React render-time setState or flushSync. Canonical upstream is /Users/avi/avir-oss/ref/base-ui at 19511bb171f3b360b006c94cf6d07e53cb446505. READ FIRST: internals/useTransitionStatus.ts and its tests, useAnimationsFinished.ts and tests, useOpenChangeComplete.tsx, useUnmountAfterClose.ts, useTriggerSwitchTransition.ts, getDisabledMountTransitionStyles.ts and utils/ItemIndicator.tsx. IMPLEMENT: Define explicit mounted/transition-status state for starting, ending, idle and undefined, respecting initially open SSR content, animateInitialOpen, optional idle state and deferred ending. Derive immediate visibility from live inputs plus owned transition state rather than mutating during render. Port finite animation discovery, starting-style observation, canceled-animation replacement handling, AbortSignal invalidation and missing-getAnimations/disabled-animation fallback. Completion callbacks must run once for the current generation and never close a reopened node. Separate logical close completion from keepMounted and preventUnmountOnClose decisions. Preserve trigger-switch transition behavior and ItemIndicator's common presence/data-attribute behavior; export the exact transition attribute names and popup/collapsible mapping leaves used by rendering. Translate the source's before-paint intent into an explicit RC13 scheduling boundary, passing completion/next-state values directly to consumers. If one narrow flush is demonstrably necessary for layout visibility, document its causal browser case rather than blanket replacing every React flushSync. Coalesced completions must recheck abort status when dequeued and must not retain Animation targets after their promises settle. WRITE BOUNDARY: listed create transition/animation/unmount stems, finite-animation and mapping/style helpers, ItemIndicator and presence coverage JSON. Renderer owns generic state mappings; positioning/popup own their composition, viewport and resizing. NON-GOALS: CSS animation library, public Collapsible/Dialog parts, geometry, global scheduler or React commit emulation. VALIDATE: translate upstream transition and animation cases with fake timers/frames and deterministic animation promises; test reopen-during-exit, initial mount, repeated cancellations, abort during queued completion and disposal. Run harness unit/type checks and retain before-paint/layout cases as deferred browser tests with exact assertions and replay instructions. Do not equate passing jsdom tests with proving browser paint order.
acceptance: Initial-open, animateInitialOpen, deferred ending and idle/undefined transitions match source observable states.
Closing stays mounted until the current completion; reopening invalidates stale animation callbacks.
Finite animation filtering, replacement after cancellation and abort/dispose races have translated tests.
Open-change completion fires once for the accepted generation and honors retained mounting policy.
No render-time setter or generic flushSync replacement exists; any narrow scheduling exception carries its proof case.
Transition attributes and ItemIndicator behavior are covered, including retained browser-only before-paint cases.

title: Port item registries, roving navigation, typeahead and composite button behavior
description: WHY: Composite lists must agree on DOM order, disabled items, active descendants and keyboard semantics across menus, tabs, radio groups and toolbars. Keep their common registry/navigation behavior independent of those public families. This is a fresh Solid 2 RC13 port of /Users/avi/avir-oss/ref/base-ui at 19511bb171f3b360b006c94cf6d07e53cb446505. READ FIRST: internals/composite/list/CompositeList.tsx, root/useCompositeRoot.ts, item/useCompositeItem.ts, composite.ts, useItemRegistry.ts and their tests; floating-ui-react/hooks/useListNavigation.ts, gridNavigation.ts and useTypeahead.ts; internals/use-button/useButton.ts. IMPLEMENT: Port createItemRegistry with an explicit live Map and immutable published snapshot so imperative registration reads do not rely on staged signal writes being visible. Preserve registration identity, automatic DOM ordering, explicit indexes, disabled metadata, text labels, wrapper moves and MutationObserver invalidation. Ref callbacks only report elements; setup-owned resources perform subscription and disposal. Implement Solid CompositeRoot/List/Item contexts using direct context providers, defaultless required lookups and explicit null optional lookup. Port roving tabindex, orientation/RTL, looping, Home/End, grid spans, virtual focus and nested floating navigation against floating-core's structural tree contract. Typeahead preserves repeated-character behavior, timeout, disabled-item skipping and native composition/key filtering. Own internal createButton and createFocusableWhenDisabled here because they consume composite context; events cannot import them without creating a dependency cycle. Preserve native/non-native keyboard activation, modifier dispatch, disabled-focusable behavior and text-navigation role exceptions. Public Button's local adapter may consume this seam once scheduled, but foundations never import the public Button directory. Re-export isElementVisible from dom-owned floating utils/visibility.ts instead of making low-level tabbable import this navigation module; preserve existing visibility checks exactly. WRITE BOUNDARY: composite/**, use-button/**, createItemRegistry.*, createFocusableWhenDisabled.*, listbox-separator/** and only the named floating navigation/typeahead/grid/composite utility files. NON-GOALS: public menu/listbox/toolbar components, selection models, popup ownership, duplicated button implementation or index-based item identity shortcuts. VALIDATE: translate registry/composite/button/navigation/typeahead suites and specs. Test simultaneous registrations, replace-and-dispose races, DOM reorders without remount, RTL and disabled navigation, virtual nested focus and changed callbacks. Run harness unit/type checks; retain WebKit and layout-dependent keyboard/focus cases for final browser replay with source titles and intended environments in coverage.
acceptance: Live registry reads include same-turn registrations while published snapshots remain stable until the scheduler publishes them.
DOM/wrapper reorder, explicit indexes and stale cleanup preserve correct item identity and metadata.
Roving/grid/virtual navigation covers RTL, loop boundaries, disabled items, Home/End and nested trees.
Typeahead timeout/repeated characters/composition cases are translated and do not recreate nodes.
Internal button behavior handles native/non-native and focusable-disabled cases without importing public Button.
Floating navigation files have one owner and no composite-to-popup/focus-manager cycle; browser-specific cases are retained.

title: Extract field/form registration and validation below public components
description: WHY: Upstream shared field registration imports validation types and helpers from public Field/Form. Reproducing those edges would make foundation and component work cyclic. Extract the engine below public families while keeping their behavior unchanged. Canonical source is /Users/avi/avir-oss/ref/base-ui at 19511bb171f3b360b006c94cf6d07e53cb446505; target is a fresh Solid 2 RC13 implementation. READ FIRST: internals/field-root-context/FieldRootContext.ts and useSetFieldFocused.ts, form-context/FormContext.ts, field-register-control/useFieldControlRegistration.ts and useRegisterFieldControl.ts, field-constants/constants.ts, field/root/useFieldValidation.ts and field/utils/getCombinedFieldValidityData.ts. IMPLEMENT: Define engine-local validity, validation-mode, form registry and control registration contracts compatible with bootstrap's facades, without runtime or type imports from target field/** or form/**. Move validation mechanics into internals/field-core/createFieldValidation.ts and the combined validity helper into that same subtree. Preserve source-token ownership, registration update-in-place order, ID/name migration, stale disposer protection, field-lifetime initial-value capture, dirty/touched/filled/focused flags and focus-owner protection. Separate plain live input/control Maps from reactive validity views; DOM nodes remain raw. Port validation debounce, async commit generations, representative invalid input selection, disabled/foreign-form exclusion, contextual portaled controls and custom validity ownership/restoration. Capture and pass next validity explicitly to form registration before staged publication. Provide optional contexts with explicit null and adapter fallbacks, not a shared mutable no-op singleton; required field-part access must throw through the approved context contract. Consume labelable-provider read-only for IDs/descriptions. Distinguish registration.value from getValue overrides and preserve the field's original baseline when a replacement control mounts later. WRITE BOUNDARY: the four listed field/form context/registration directories plus internals/field-core/** and coverage JSON. Public Field, Fieldset, Form and controls own their rendering, submission shells and indexes; providers owns labelable registration. NON-GOALS: public component implementation, field-specific UI, importing public FieldRoot types, duplicated validation engines or automatic prop-to-store sync. VALIDATE: translate relevant Field/Form regression cases into engine fixtures, retaining source titles. Cover async stale results, control replacement, baseline across remount, multiple invalid group inputs, external invalid errors and native custom-message restoration. Run harness type/unit checks and preserve browser native-validity, focus and portal-form cases for final integration replay using real component families.
acceptance: Core has no runtime or type import from public field, form, fieldset or control directories.
Re-registration preserves Map order and initial baseline; replaced control cleanup cannot delete the current registration.
Async/debounced stale validation cannot overwrite newer values or disposed fields.
Disabled/foreign-form exclusion and contextual portaled participation match source eligibility rules.
Custom validity restoration, group representative input selection and explicit next validity publication are tested.
Optional null contexts and required failures are correct; public families receive typed engine contracts and retained integration cases.

title: Port direction, CSP and labelable providers with acyclic context ownership
description: WHY: Direction, CSP and label ownership cross component boundaries and portals. Their reactive values must not become setup-time snapshots or require Field/Form to exist first. Use only /Users/avi/avir-oss/ref/base-ui at 19511bb171f3b360b006c94cf6d07e53cb446505 as behavioral upstream for this fresh Solid 2 RC13 port. READ FIRST: internals/direction-context/DirectionContext.tsx, csp-context/CSPContext.tsx, labelable-provider/LabelableProvider.tsx and LabelableContext.ts; direction-provider/DirectionProvider.tsx, csp-provider/CSPProvider.tsx, internals/PrehydrationScript.tsx and utils/styles.tsx. IMPLEMENT: Use the context value directly as provider JSX, never .Provider. Direction defaults to ltr while nested live values override it; CSP retains nonce and disableStyleElements semantics. Optional contexts are explicitly createContext<T | null>(null), with immutable fallback adapters at the consumption seam; required contexts use the defaultless form and its missing-provider failure. Port LabelableProvider with source-token control registration, stable current selection across registration churn, intentional null suppression of label for, and undefined removal. Generated IDs come exclusively from lifecycle's verified mechanism. Preserve parent/child message ID aggregation, duplicate removal, description order and registered-label cleanup. Implement createLabelableId/createAriaLabelledBy/createLabel, registered-label and aria-label resolution utilities using current props. Extract effect compute inputs and return registration cleanup; ref application creates no owners. Port CSP-aware style injection and PrehydrationScript's server-body/client-stub structural contract using RC13-supported SSR behavior, proving the hydration structure instead of copying suppressHydrationWarning. Bootstrap owns conditional package import mappings and receives exact requested entries. Style insertion must not rely on React's href/precedence hoisting; prove deduplication, ordering and disposal under the actual Solid renderer. WRITE BOUNDARY: direction/csp/labelable internal subtrees, both public provider directories, named label/style/prehydration helpers and providers coverage JSON. Field/form contexts belong only to field-core; floating/portal contexts belong to their respective owners. NON-GOALS: public Field parts, global theme system, private hydration internals, ID counters or root barrel edits. VALIDATE: translate provider and label tests; cover nested live direction, nonce changes, style suppression, control replacement, null labels and inherited descriptions. Run harness unit/type and minimal SSR structural checks. Retain actual script-before-hydration and cross-portal provider cases with explicit final-browser replay instructions rather than removing the source cases.
acceptance: Provider JSX uses Context directly; optional contexts use explicit null and required lookups fail without a provider.
Nested direction/CSP updates remain reactive without remounting children or effect-syncing props.
Label registrations distinguish null from undefined, preserve selection and ignore stale cleanup.
ARIA descriptions retain inherited/local/external ordering and deduplicate IDs.
CSP nonce and disableStyleElements are honored; prehydration script structure has an RC13-supported proof and export-import handoff.
No field/form/floating runtime ownership leaks into this task; translated and deferred cases are recorded.

title: Establish floating root/tree contracts without popup or geometry cycles
description: WHY: Floating interactions, composite navigation, focus, geometry and popup models all need a common root/tree. A dedicated owner avoids granting several workers the whole floating-ui-react directory and breaks upstream store imports back into popup utilities. Canonical source is /Users/avi/avir-oss/ref/base-ui at 19511bb171f3b360b006c94cf6d07e53cb446505, translated directly to Solid 2 RC13. READ FIRST: floating-ui-react/components/FloatingRootStore.ts, FloatingTreeStore.ts, FloatingTree.tsx, hooks/useFloatingRootContext.ts and useSyncedFloatingRootContext.ts, types.ts, utils/createEventEmitter.ts, getEmptyRootContext.ts and nodes.ts. IMPLEMENT: Replace ReactStore subclasses with createFloatingRoot/createFloatingTree owned models using accessors/signals and plain imperative metadata.
